newsitem.title: USA: Clinton calls jobless rate "good news".
newsitem.headline: Clinton calls jobless rate "good news".

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton on Friday hailed the drop in the nation's jobless rate as "good news" that showed that the U.S. economy was on the right track.
"The American economy, my fellow Americans, is on the right track," Clinton said during a speech in Florida to a gathering of black religious leaders.

Citing "more good news," Clinton pointed to new unemployment figures released early in Washington that showed the nation's jobless rate was 5.1 percent and stressed it underscored the overall health of the economy. "We must keep it going," he said.
He said the figures were "just the latest evidence of strong growth, the highest consumer confidence in years...our unemployment has dropped to its lowest level in seven and a half years."

The decline in the unemployment rate, which was especially steep among workers over 55 and in their early 20s, brought the jobless rate to its lowest level since March 1989 when it was 5.0 percent, the Labour Department reported.
Clinton was campaigning for re-election with a series of appearances in Florida.
